messages.author: 74c72f24da30ebe7
messages.subject: NA's for yearly site covariates
parts:
Hello all,

I am using colext to analyze a multiseason dataset in which I include yearly site covariates as predictor variables for colonization and extinction.

I did not survey all points in all years.

I documented the yearly site covariates when I conducted a survey. Therefore, if I did not conduct a survey at a site in a given year, I only have NA for the yearly site covariate. If I run my models with the NA's I get the error: 
Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = getHessian, ...) : 
  initial value in 'vmmin' is not finite

I have tried multiple different starting values, but always get the error.

However, if I convert the NA's to a number (either mode of all years of the known data (= 0) or mean of all years of the known data (= 209), the models run fine. Regardless of whether I use the mode or mean, The results are similar (same order from modSel, similar, but not exactly the same delta AIC weight, coef, etc.).

A few questions:
1) Why would the yearly site covariates for sites which were not visited affect the results? 
2) Knowing that they do affect the results, would it be wrong to substitute a number for the NA's?
3) If it seems OK to substitute a number, would mean of all years, mode of all years, mean of the year with the na, or mode of the year with the na make the most sense? (The covariates are quite different for each    site in a given year, and for each site over the years.)

This seems like it would be a common problem...

Thank you!

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] NA's for yearly site covariates
parts:
Hi Taza,

Perhaps the best thing to do would be to put a prior on the missing covariate values and integrate over them. You can't do this in unmarked, but it is easy to do in JAGS.  

If there are only a few missing covariates, then it might not be too problematic to stick with unmarked and impute them using one of the methods you suggested above. The only way to understand the effect of your imputation choice would be to conduct a simulation study.

Richard

messages.author: caaac2dc0aae28b8
messages.subject: Re: NA's for yearly site covariates
parts:
Hello;
I'm trying to understand the implications of missing a site for an entire season in a multi-season occupancy study on colonization and extinction parameter estimation. Based on this example, it appears that colext will not work when yearly site covariates (yearlySiteCovs) with missing years are included on gamma or epsilon. I did not expect this but instead thought that those observations would just not be used in parameter estimation. Can anyone tell me if  there is a fundamental reason that missing seasons for yearly site covariates causes estimation problems for colonization and extinction, or is this just a limitation in how the estimation is done in unmarked?
Thanks,
Eric Stolen

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: NA's for yearly site covariates
parts:
I'd like to suggest that this isn't a limitation of colext but rather that it is impossible to determine the joint probability of the true (and therefore also of the observed) status of the remaining years because the joint probability must include parameters dependent on the covariates of the missing years.  All that colext could possibly do is give a more explicit warning or perform some imputation process (and notify the user that this was done) or ignore observations from the missing year and on for that site.  (Even the latter might have issues if the missingness is related to the value of the covariate.)

I've attached a pdf document describing this issue for 3 seasons when season 2 covariates are missing.

And if I'm all wet with this rationale, please be gentle with responses.

Jim
